"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. Only the training recipe can change. The default recipe collects 4,096 samples per update, which gives only 32 PPO updates in the 131k-step budget, while the learning rate decays linearly to zero. The 4-seed baseline is 0.068 three times and 0.258 once, so training sometimes takes off and usually does not. That points to too few policy improvements, not too little capacity. Cutting PPO epochs buys more samples: 1 epoch gives about 426k steps and 2 epochs about 243k. Round 1 therefore tests three ways to add updates or samples: (1) the same samples split into smaller batches, giving 4 times as many updates; (2) 1 epoch with 3.25 times as many samples and many updates; (3) 2 epochs plus a longer reward horizon (gamma 0.99), because the +1 exact-build bonus comes up to 20 placements after the early choices. Each trial runs 2 seeds, and a mean change of about 0.1 can still be seed noise.
analyses.2: The 0.068 result looks like a stable plateau: five of the eight seeds outside r1c1 landed on exactly 0.0684, and four of those came from the one-epoch and two-epoch trials. Only r1c1 got both seeds clear of it (0.158 and 0.207), using 4 epochs, 64 environments and 128 updates. r1c2 and r1c3 used the same 64-sample minibatches and a similar number of gradient steps (6.6k and 7.6k, against 8.2k for r1c1), but reused each sample only once or twice, and both stayed on the plateau. So reusing samples more often, together with frequent policy updates, seems to be what matters. Adding fresh samples by cutting epochs did not help. This round keeps r1c1's setup and changes one thing in each candidate: 8 epochs (more reuse), learning rate 0.002 (faster learning), and rollout length 8 (twice as many updates). A gain needs to be well above r1c1's spread between seeds to count.
analyses.3: Doubling lr to 0.002 on r1c1's small-batch setup (64 envs, 128 updates) lifted dev success from about 0.18 to 0.62. Both seeds came in at 0.53 and 0.72. The gap from the 0.116 baseline is far larger than seed noise, so step size is the main lever we have found. The batch-size change (r1c1) gave a smaller gain that may still be real. Changing epochs (r2c1, 8 epochs), rollout length (r2c3) or fewer epochs with more samples did not help at lr 0.001. Those runs mostly stayed at the 0.068 plateau, so they tell us little about other settings once learning actually takes off. At lr 0.001 the policy probably learned too slowly within the budget. Next: push lr to the 0.003 cap. Then re-test the horizon (gamma 0.99) and lower entropy at lr 0.002, each as a single change. That way round 4 can combine whatever wins.
analyses.4: The learning rate has the biggest effect. With 64 envs, rollout 16 and 16 minibatches, raising lr from 0.001 to 0.002 lifted dev success from 0.18 to 0.62. lr 0.003 was worse (0.45), so the best rate is probably near 0.002. Raising gamma to 0.99 gave 0.657, the current best, but its seeds were 0.79 and 0.52, so the gain over r2c2 is within noise. Lowering entropy to 0.002 hurt (0.42), and one of its seeds was weak. Doubling the epochs or halving the rollout at lr 0.001 changed nothing. One epoch, and large batches at the default lr, stayed stuck at 0.068. Seed spread is still about ±0.13, so these are 2-seed means only. This is the last round, so each candidate makes one change to r3c2 and should not risk collapse. The three changes are a longer GAE horizon, slightly fewer epochs to get more fresh designs, and a higher entropy bonus, the opposite of the setting that failed.
